newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge in split ruling on tobacco documents.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge in split ruling on tobacco documents.

text.p: The judge in Florida's lawsuit against the tobacco industry on Friday ruled that pretrial questioning of witnesses based on internal industry documents would remain secret for now.

But Judge Harold Cohen of the Palm Beach County Circuit Court at the same hearing rejected a tobacco industry request that some 800 industry documents already widely disseminated on the Internet and elsewhere be sealed.

The split decision allows lawyers for the state of Florida to use any industry documents they have, including some unidentified papers that have not been made public, in deposing witnesses in the lead-up to a scheduled August 4 trial.

Florida is claiming more than $1 billion in damages from U.S. cigarette companies and the Brown & Williamson unit of B.A.T Industries Plc for costs of treating people with smoking-related illnesses under the state's Medicaid health program.

Eighteen other states are also suing the tobacco industry to recoup Medicaid costs for treating smokers. Alabama's lieutenant governor filed a private lawsuit against the industry, and Alaska recently said it was seriously considering a lawsuit.
